laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in Nunavut is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from private licensed stores, in person and online.

Auyuittuq National Park: travel is designated hazardous; every visitor must register (in person or by phone) before entering and de-register after leaving (not Nunavut Inuit harvesting); maximum fine C$100,000. Fees: daily C$17.75 (about A$18.04 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) per person, nightly C$37, annual C$259; youth 17 and under free.

laws.rule: Cannabis Act, S.Nu. 2018, c.7, s. 35(1): nobody may consume cannabis in, on, or within a regulated distance of a hospital or health facility, a school, a child day care facility (or a home providing paid child care while it is operating), a playground, sports field, arena, community hall or recreation centre, a public place where goods or services are sold to the public (other than a cannabis lounge), or a parade, concert or other public event. The distance is set by regulation, which this entry has not read. Hotel and motel rooms used for sleeping only are exempt (s. 35(7)). Section 36 bans smoking any substance, including in your own dwelling, in a way that lets smoke or vapour reach a workplace, public place, apartment or condominium common area, or another dwelling without the occupant's consent. The consolidation read is marked current to 25 September 2020, so later amendments may apply.

Under the same Act, a person may import cannabis into Nunavut only by purchase from a remote sales store, or as personal effects when travelling to Nunavut, up to the amount lawfully allowed to be possessed in a public place (s. 24(1)). Buying, possessing or consuming illicit cannabis is banned (s. 26(1)), and a minor may not provide, buy, possess or consume cannabis (s. 31).

items.text: The legal age for cannabis in Nunavut is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy from private licensed stores, in person or online.
Cannabis may be used in a private residence or a licensed smoke lounge; you can't smoke it in most public places.

Under the updated Tobacco and Smoking Act it's illegal to smoke, vape or use cannabis in a motorised vehicle (car, boat, ATV or snowmobile) when anyone under 19 is present, within 9 m of building entrances, or in Government of Nunavut staff and public housing.

The legal drinking age is 19. Each community is under one of three liquor systems: prohibited (buying, importing or drinking any alcohol there is illegal), restricted (a local Alcohol Education Committee controls orders and imports) or unrestricted. Government pages list some communities differently, so check a community's current system with the Nunavut Liquor and Cannabis Commission before bringing alcohol.

layers.process: Parks Canada's Auyuittuq page says: if you plan to travel on Inuit-owned land, you must contact the Qikiqtani Inuit Association to obtain permission. This is the Qikiqtani (Baffin) region; other Nunavut regions have their own Inuit land administration, not yet checked. Whether permission is given is the Association's decision.

Backcountry fees per person: CAD 17.75 a day excursion with no overnight stay (about A$18.04 (A$1 = CAD 0.9838, RBA 30 Oct 2026)); CAD 37.00 a night camping (about A$37.61); CAD 259.00 annual northern park permit (about A$263.27). Weatherhaven semi-private accommodation CAD 37.25 a night single or CAD 31.00 double. Youth 17 and under enter free but the backcountry permit still applies. The park is most easily reached by charter aircraft from Resolute Bay and is most accessible from May to August; visitors must be experienced and self-reliant. Registration steps are not on the web pages read: contact the Parks Canada Resolute office, 1-867-252-3000, nunavut.info@pc.gc.ca.
